title: Range, Variance and Standard Deviation
seo_title: Measures of Dispersion – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the range, mean deviation, variance and standard deviation of ungrouped and grouped data; compare spreads. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on measures of dispersion: range, mean deviation, variance and standard deviation for lists and frequency tables. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A bigger SD means more spread.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Range = highest − lowest.
  • Variance = mean of the squared deviations; standard deviation = √variance.
  • Adding the same number to every value does not change the SD; multiplying every value by k multiplies the SD by k.

Examples

Example

2, 4, 6

Mean 4

Deviations −2, 0, 2

(4 + 0 + 4) ÷ 3

Answer: SD = √(8/3) ≈ 1.63

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to square root the varianceSD = √variance.
Using Σx² ÷ n − x̄ wronglySquare the mean: Σx²/n − x̄².
Ignoring the signs of deviationsSquare them so they are all positive.

faq.q: What does a small SD mean?
faq.a: The data is close to the mean.
The mean of the distances from the mean.
